speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
text: asked	the Minister for the Environment and Water Resources in addition to a letter written by the CEO of NEA to his counterpart in Indonesia, what other steps will the Ministry take to address the haze issue in anticipation of worsening haze conditions.

speaker: The Minister for the Environment and Water Resources (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: The advisories contain useful information, such as the air quality forecast for the following day with a corresponding health advisory and information pertaining to the hotspots situation.

speaker: The Minister for the Environment and Water Resources (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: This will allow the public to plan ahead for their activities.

speaker: The Minister for the Environment and Water Resources (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: We have also been working with the Indonesian Government at regional fora, such as Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN), to explore initiatives that can help address the haze issue.

speaker: The Minister for the Environment and Water Resources (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: We were also active in ensuring the full and effective implementation of the ASEAN Agreement on Transboundary Haze Pollution, as well as pushing for the expeditious operationalisation of the ASEAN Haze Monitoring System.

speaker: The Minister for the Environment and Water Resources (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Ultimately, we recognise that transboundary haze is a manmade and commercially driven issue.

speaker: The Minister for the Environment and Water Resources (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Consumers in Singapore should send similar signals to influence companies to adopt environmentally sustainable practices that do not Page: 35 contribute to smoke haze.

speaker: The Minister for the Environment and Water Resources (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: I am heartened that some non-government organisations have stepped up their support in this regard.

speaker: The Minister for the Environment and Water Resources (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: For example, the World Wildlife Fund Singapore (WWF-SG) has recently established the Singapore Alliance for Sustainable Palm Oil to encourage businesses here to use certified palm oil which does not contribute to the haze in its production.

speaker: The Minister for the Environment and Water Resources (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: I encourage all stakeholders to persevere in our efforts to combat the haze.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Will the Ministry also consider using other internationally recognised standards, such as the Forest Stewardship Council's (FSC) certification?

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: Indeed, we are concerned that standards should exist so that companies, big or small, have guidance what to buy, where to buy from and therefore, the WWF-SG's Singapore Alliance for Sustainable Palm Oil standard is one of the standards that we are hoping will be one that will resonate with the industry.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: There are others, like the Roundtable on Sustainable Palm Oil, and they have different standards and means of implementation, but we welcome them all.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: The Singapore Green Label for paper is only one of the product categories that the Singapore Environment Council (SEC) is producing.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: It is a primary means to ensure that it is more comprehensive and will give those egregious companies a chance for them to make good to practise sustainable production.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: FSC is also a label that SEC recognises but it is not as comprehensive as the Singapore Green Label.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: And while the Singapore Green Label will take some time to mature, FSC is a good enough standard for us to rely on.

speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (Jurong)
text: Could the Minister update what is the latest assistance that Singapore has offered to fight fires in the forests of Indonesia and whether our offers are taken up by Indonesia?
